person: Lorna Pike is the 58-year-old office and compliance manager at a small importer that runs its own trucks. She sends original customs documents, permits and replacement parts overnight on two parcel carriers, and she has handled claims for 22 years. Late parcels pile up in the shipping app and the inbox, and she wants to file only the claims the carriers' own guarantees support. She has no patience for a tool that guesses, and she was burned by a freight-audit vendor that kept a share of every recovery and botched two claims. She wants each claim to show its line, its rule and its source, and she wants any practice run labeled as one.
stated_up_front: I have a batch of late overnight parcels from the last few weeks on both carriers. Go through them and file only the ones where the carrier's own guarantee applies, and show me the rule and the line for each one. Don't send me any 'potential savings' total.

facts.truth: Priority Overnight envelope of entry documents to the broker, scheduled Wed 14 Oct by 10:30, delivered Thu 15 Oct at 11:20. Transportation charge $48.60, business address, no address or tender problem.
15 days from the scheduled delivery date, so the 14 Oct parcel can be claimed through 29 Oct.
An overnight box to a customer in Tennessee arrived a day late on 8 Oct, during the thunderstorms in Wrenpost's service alert. Charge $61.20.

facts.about: Wrenpost Ground parcel to leave alone
facts.truth: A Ground carton of gaskets, 3 days late, charge $22.40. Ground's guarantee is suspended, so no claim.

Lane Next-Day parcel of a replacement pump part to a business address, scheduled Mon 12 Oct, delivered Tue 13 Oct at 2:05 pm. Transportation charge $37.85. It appears on the weekly invoice dated 19 Oct.
15 days from the invoice date, so the invoice dated 19 Oct runs to 3 Nov. An earlier invoice dated 21 Sep has already closed, on 6 Oct.

facts.about: Lanecourier parcel to leave alone (late drop-off)
facts.truth: A parcel handed to the driver at 6:40 pm, after the 5:30 pm cut-off, so it was on time for its moved commitment. Charge $41.10.
A permit original sent with an adult signature required to the Ferncastle office. Nobody was there to sign, and Mailnest has the recipient's email saying so. Charge $44.00.
One Lanecourier Next-Day parcel was credited $39.50 on the 5 Oct invoice. Her own Outlook note, 'asked for credit 28 Sep, got it', confirms it.
Mailnest has an offer from a freight-audit service that keeps 50% of every refund. She will not use it, and it is the same kind of vendor that burned her two years ago.

unknowns: Which of the carrier's service levels have the guarantee suspended, and for how long.
Whether the carriers allow any tolerance (in seconds or minutes) before a parcel counts as late.
Why one parcel's label lacked a suite number, and whether the carrier or the shipping app's address check dropped it.
What the carrier's internal exception codes on the tracking mean.
